note: Definition of terms shown in the vault's Glossary. Groups appear in this order; terms are sorted A to Z inside each group. Edit here, then run tools/build_desktop.py.

groups.name: Search Basics
groups.about: Everyday SEO words used in reports and audits.
terms: Improving a website so it shows up higher in Google's free (organic) results.
The page Google shows after a search: ads, the map pack, AI Overviews and the organic links.
Visitors who arrive from free search results, not from paid ads.
A word or phrase people type into Google, such as "sewer line repair mesa".
The one main keyword a page or blog is built around. It should appear in the title and H1.
About how many times a keyword is searched per month.
What the searcher wants: to learn something (informational), compare options (commercial) or hire someone now (transactional).
How many times a page appeared in search results, even if nobody clicked.
Clicks divided by impressions. A 5% CTR means 5 clicks for every 100 times the page was shown.
Where a page shows in the results for a keyword. Position 1 is the top organic result.
Keywords ranking just off the top spots (about positions 8 to 20). Small improvements can move them onto page one.
Quick wins: pages or keywords that need only a small fix to gain traffic.
A link from another website to yours. Good links from trusted sites help rankings.
The clickable words of a link. It tells Google what the linked page is about.
Two or more of your own pages competing for the same keyword, so neither ranks well.
A search that includes the business name, such as "Pipeliners Mesa".

groups.name: Local SEO and Google Business Profile
groups.about: Ranking in Google Maps and the local map pack.
terms: SEO for businesses that serve a specific area, focused on Google Maps and "near me" searches.
The free Google listing that shows a business on Maps and in the map pack, with reviews, hours, photos and posts.
The box of three businesses with a map that Google shows for local searches.
The business name, address and phone number. They must match exactly everywhere online.
A listing of the business NAP on another site, such as Yelp, Bing Places or Apple Maps.
The main GBP category (for example Plumber). It has the biggest effect on which searches a profile shows for.
A business that travels to customers instead of serving them at a storefront.
Google's three local ranking factors: how close the business is, how well it matches the search, and how well known and trusted it is.
A map of rank checks across a grid of points around the business, showing where it ranks in the top 3 (green) and where it doesn't.
A website page about a service in one city, such as "Drain Cleaning in Tempe".
A short update published on the Google Business Profile, like a mini social post.
How steadily new Google reviews come in over time.
From the Modern SEO course: a website page for every GBP category and service, linked the way the GBP is organized.
From the Modern SEO course: fix the GBP, fix the GBP landing page, then build verified citations.

groups.name: AI Search
groups.about: Getting found and quoted by AI answer engines.
terms: Shaping content so search engines and voice assistants can pull a direct answer from it.
Shaping content so AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity mention and cite the business.
The AI-written summary Google shows at the top of some search results.
Google's chat-style search mode that answers with AI and cites sources.
The kind of AI behind ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.
When an AI answer names or links to a business or page as its source.
The extra searches an AI tool runs behind the scenes to answer one question.
A plain text file on a website that summarizes the business for AI crawlers.
A search answered right on the results page, so the person never clicks a website.

groups.name: Technical SEO
groups.about: How Google crawls, reads and indexes a site.
terms: Google's bots visiting pages to read them.
Google storing a page so it can appear in search. A page that isn't indexed can't rank.
A GSC status: Google knows the page exists but hasn't crawled it yet.
A GSC status: Google read the page but chose not to add it to search, often because it looks thin or duplicated.
A file listing a site's pages so search engines can find them.
A file that tells crawlers which parts of a site they may or may not visit.
A tag that tells Google not to show a page in search results.
A tag that says which URL is the main version when similar pages exist.
A permanent forward from an old URL to a new one that passes along most of its ranking value.
The page title shown as the blue headline in search results.
The short summary under the title in search results. It affects clicks, not rankings.
The main heading on a page. A page should have exactly one.
A short description of an image for screen readers and search engines.
Hidden code that tells search engines facts about a page, such as business details, FAQs or services.
The code format Google recommends for schema markup.
Schema that describes a local business: name, address, phone, hours and service area.
Schema listing questions and answers. It must match the FAQ text visible on the page.
A link from one page to another page on the same website.
A page no other page on the site links to, which makes it hard for Google to find.
Google's page experience scores for loading speed, responsiveness and layout stability.
How fast a page loads, often measured with Google PageSpeed Insights.

groups.name: Content
groups.about: Blogs, pages and how they fit together.
terms: A long main page on a broad topic that links out to related, more specific posts.
A pillar page plus the supporting posts that link back to it.
A post that answers one narrower question and links up to its pillar or service page.
The plan for a page before writing: keyword, intent, outline, questions to answer and links.
Many similar pages built from one template, such as one page per city.
A near-copy page made only to rank for one place or keyword. Google treats these as spam.
A page with too little useful or unique information to deserve ranking.
Qualities Google looks for in content, especially real first-hand experience.
WordPress's built-in block editor, used for most Pipeliners blogs.

groups.name: Google Ads and Tracking
terms: Google's paid advertising platform. TAG's Google Ads accounts are read-only for Claude.
A Google Ads account that manages several client accounts. TAG's is 805-257-4115.
The top level of a Google Ads account, with its own budget, locations and goals.
A set of keywords and ads inside a campaign.
The exact searches that triggered an ad, which can differ from the keywords.
A word or phrase that stops ads showing for unwanted searches.
How closely a search must match a keyword to show the ad: broad, phrase or exact.
A tracked action that counts as a result, such as a call, form fill or booked job.
The setting in Google Ads that defines and counts one type of conversion.
A conversion uploaded later from the CRM, such as a call that became a real lead.
A code Google adds to ad clicks so a later lead can be matched back to the ad.
What each ad click costs on average.
Ad spend divided by conversions: what each lead costs.
Google's website analytics tool for visits, sources and events.
A tool for adding tracking codes to a website without editing the site's code.
Call tracking that swaps the phone number shown on the site to see which source drove the call.
Tags added to a link (utm_source, utm_medium and so on) so analytics knows where a visit came from.
The field in the CRM that records where a lead came from.

groups.name: Tools and Platforms
groups.about: Software used across TAG client work.
terms: The SEO platform TAG uses for site audits, rank tracking, keyword research and OTTO.
Search Atlas's automation that pushes SEO changes (titles, metas, schema, alt text) to a live site. It can override what WordPress shows.
The Search Atlas WordPress plugin that connects a site to OTTO.
Google's free tool showing indexing, search queries, clicks and errors for a site.
The CRM and marketing platform TAG clients use for contacts, call tracking and automations.
TAG's internal work CRM for tasks (keystone.so).
A lead tracking tool that records calls and forms and can send conversions to Google Ads.
An AI image and video generation platform. Generations use paid credits.
A paid local SEO tool for rank maps, GBP management and citations, mentioned in the Modern SEO course.
A desktop crawler that lists every page on a site with its titles, links and errors.
A WordPress SEO plugin for titles, metas and schema. Summit AZ uses it.
Another WordPress SEO plugin, used on some sites before Rank Math or Search Atlas.
A drag-and-drop WordPress page builder used for many client pages.
The website platform behind most client sites.
A command line tool for managing WordPress from the server.
Anthropic's AI coding assistant, used to research, write and build for TAG.
A free note app that stores notes as plain Markdown files. TAG Brain is an Obsidian vault.
The online community platform that hosts the Modern SEO course.

groups.name: Websites and Hosting
groups.about: Where sites live and how they are changed.
terms: A website's address, such as pipelinersusa.com.
The server where a website's files and database live (for example NameHero, SiteGround or Hostinger).
A secure way to log in to a server's command line.
Saved copies of pages that make a site load faster. It must be cleared after changes or visitors may see the old version.
A private copy of a website for testing changes before they go live.
A WordPress plugin that always runs and can't be switched off from the dashboard.
A website made of plain HTML files with no database, like Prestige Plumbing's site.
A project folder tracked with Git, often stored on GitHub.
Publishing a new version of a website or app so people can use it.

groups.name: Trenchless and Plumbing
terms: Repairing pipes without digging a long trench, usually through one or two small access points.
Installing a new pipe inside the old one. Pipeliners copy says "lining the pipe", never "pipelining".
A resin-soaked liner pushed into the old pipe and hardened with heat or UV light.
A coating sprayed inside water pipes to stop pinhole leaks. Pipeliners offers it.
Cleaning drains with very high pressure water.
Sending a camera through a pipe to see cracks, roots and blockages.
Breaking the old pipe while pulling a new one through. Pipeliners does not offer it.
A leak in a water line under the concrete floor of a house.
An old pipe made of tar and wood pulp that breaks down over time.
Replacing a home's water pipes. Pipeliners does not offer full repipes.
A capped opening in the sewer line used to access and clean the pipe.

groups.name: Vault and Files
groups.about: Words and badges used inside this vault.
terms: This app: Kim's prompts, lessons, notes and tools in one place.
The Obsidian notes folder that summarizes everything in the TAG Marketing Claude folder. It appears in the vault's TAG Brain section.
A note that links to everything about one client or topic.
An Obsidian link written as [[Note name]]. In the vault it becomes a normal link.
The details block at the top of an Obsidian note: type, client, tags, source and date.
The box under a TAG Brain note's title showing the folder or file it came from.
The star map of every page: dots are notes and lines are links between them.
Kim's daily summary of work done, grouped by client.
Step-by-step instructions for a repeatable task.
A summary written so the next work session can pick up where the last one stopped.
A folder that holds other files and folders. (Computers also call this a directory.)
A Markdown note: plain text with simple formatting like # headings and - bullets.
Spreadsheet data saved as plain text, with values separated by commas or tabs.
An image file (PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF or SVG).
A structured data file used by apps and scripts.
A script or code file (Python, JavaScript, PHP, PowerShell or shell).
A compressed archive holding other files.
